about.title: about
paragraphs: I'm a software engineer and researcher. I build intelligent AI systems, from automating the software development lifecycle (SDLC) to making teaching and learning smoother for professors and students. Basically, I make machines do the boring work so humans don't have to.

Now I'm doing my Master's in Computer Science (Research) at the University at Buffalo - SUNY, pursuing supervised research under Prof. Junsong Yuan (Chair, CSE) on human motion generation. Basically, I teach computers how people move. They keep giving humans three knees. I tried blockchain once, then agentic AI and LLMs showed up and I never looked back.
Off the keyboard: badminton and cricket. Same energy, worse aim. Say hi at rpandey3@buffalo.edu or pandeyraunak1007@gmail.com.

items.name: GoingOnce
items.description: won 1st place in the ACV Auctions challenge at UB's AI for Good hackathon (Oct 2026). Four AI agents built with LangGraph and Claude help car dealers buy, sell, negotiate and move fleet cars, built by my team in a single five-hour sprint.
items.detailedDescription:
1st place in the ACV Auctions + Copart challenge at AI for Good, Fall 2026, a hackathon hosted by UB's Startup and Innovation Collaboratory on October 3, 2026. We had 10:30 AM to 3:30 PM to build it.

The idea: every car finds its best buyer, across ACV and Copart. Four AI agents, one for each part of a car dealer's day:
  • Buy: a dealer says what they need in plain words. The agent searches ACV and Copart, checks each car's history, throws out cars with hidden damage, and asks before bidding.
  • Sell: photos in. AI writes the condition report, shows where the seller keeps the most money, and finds buyers already waiting.
  • Negotiate: each side's agent keeps a private limit, and a mediator closes the gap in rounds. Then the deal closes itself: payment, insurance, title, truck.
  • Fleet: a rental fleet selling 120 similar cars gets spread across markets in full truckloads, so prices hold and transport stays cheap.
Team: Raunak Kumar Pandey, Vedant Shinde, Aniket Khade, Jay Pathare.

Stack: Python · LangGraph · Claude · Streamlit · FastAPI · React

Read the story of how we won →

items.name: PatchPilot
items.description: is an AI agent I built to help with my own open-source contributions. It figures out unfamiliar repos through retrieval over source code and Git history, then writes working patches for GitHub issues. Built with Python, LangGraph, LangSmith, RAG, Qdrant and MCP.
items.detailedDescription:
PatchPilot started because I wanted to contribute to open source faster, without spending days just understanding a new codebase. (Jun - Aug 2026)

What it does:
  • Reads an unfamiliar repository using retrieval over its source code and Git history
  • Generates working code patches for open GitHub issues
  • Follows policy guardrails so it doesn't go rogue on someone's repo
  • Runs run-level evaluation to check how well each attempt did
Stack: Python · LangGraph · LangSmith · RAG · Qdrant · MCP

items.name: De novo Peptide Sequencing
items.description: reads protein sequences straight from mass spectrometry data, even for unknown organisms hiding in wastewater. I worked on InstaNovo (transformers) and InstaNovo+ (diffusion-based refinement). Presented at CSE Demo Day 2026.
items.detailedDescription:
A deep learning project on de novo peptide sequencing from tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) data, presented at UB CSE Demo Day 2026.

Wastewater samples can contain proteins from many unknown organisms that aren't in any reference database, so we can't just look them up. We compared Casanovo, Novor, InstaNovo and InstaNovo+.

My part:
  • InstaNovo: predicts peptide sequences from spectra with transformers
  • InstaNovo+: refines those predictions with a diffusion-transformer model
Evaluation: precision and recall on E. coli vesicle proteomics data, and false discovery rate (FDR) plus biological interpretation with UniPept on wastewater samples.

Built with my teammate Swati Bhatt, guided by Prof. Mingchen Gao.

Stack: PyTorch · Transformers · Diffusion models

items.name: Human Skeleton Joint Inpainting
items.description: rebuilds missing elbow and knee joints on human skeletons using a DDIM diffusion model, reaching hole PSNR 22.20 and hole L1 0.09 on COCO keypoints. Built with PyTorch, OpenCV and diffusion models.
items.detailedDescription:
The sequel to my MNIST inpainting project. Once the model could fill holes in digits, I gave it a harder job: people.

I masked the elbow and knee joints on COCO keypoint skeletons and trained a DDIM diffusion model in PyTorch to reconstruct them. (Nov 2025 - Feb 2026)

Results (measured inside the masked joints):
  • PSNR: 22.20
  • L1: 0.09
Stack: PyTorch · OpenCV · Diffusion models

items.name: DDIM Inpainting on MNIST
items.description: was my diffusion warm-up. I cut a hole in the center of MNIST digits and trained a timestep-conditioned U-Net to fill it back in with DDIM sampling. This is what led to the skeleton project.
items.detailedDescription:
My first diffusion project. I trained a timestep-conditioned U-Net diffusion model on MNIST digits with the center masked out, then reconstructed the missing region with DDIM sampling.

To keep it honest, evaluation only counts pixels inside the hole: hole-only PSNR and hole-only L1 (MAE).

It worked well enough that I moved on to human skeletons next.

Stack: PyTorch · Diffusion models (DDIM) · U-Net

items.name: eBay 2025 ML Competition: Automotive NER
items.description: pulls car part details out of German eBay product titles. Scored a 0.869 weighted F-score (beta = 0.2) by training XLM-RoBERTa with BIOES tagging on 9K labeled plus 2M unlabeled titles. Built with Python, NLP and XLM-RoBERTa.
items.detailedDescription:
eBay car part titles are short, messy and full of abbreviations: OEM codes, sizes, random casing. This project turns raw German titles into structured entities, which helps with better search, cleaner product attributes, and smarter cataloging and recommendations. (Jul - Oct 2025)

Data: about 2M unlabeled German motor-vehicle part titles, plus 9K hand-labeled samples with token-level entity tags.

How:
  • Cleaned up whitespace, special characters, German abbreviations and casing, with rules for units (mm, inch), part numbers and OEM codes
  • Converted the labels to the BIOES scheme (Begin, Inside, Outside, End, Single)
  • Fine-tuned FacebookAI/xlm-roberta-large as a token classifier with token-level cross-entropy
Result: 0.869172 weighted F0.2. The metric uses beta = 0.2, so precision matters much more than recall. Better to be right than to guess.

Stack: Python · PyTorch · Hugging Face Transformers · XLM-RoBERTa
